svg.title: Image in-context read: the full data flow of LabelledRead.forward for one table, every tensor with its shape, every operation, with the tensors that involve labels in yellow and the content-only ones in purple

g.text: Image in-context read (LabelledRead.forward): every tensor and operation of one table's forward pass
ModelConfig: width 128, 4 heads, 2 layers, up to 256 sources, top-32; shapes for one table, (photos, patches, width) with the batch axis dropped
context photos first, then test photos
the context rows' labels; no test label
past 256: a random subset per training step
one label embedding per source photo
h, the stage input, also feeds the reads directly
nearest_photos(h, sources, k = 32): retrieval, no weights, once per table on the stage input
32 or fewer sources N = None and every patch
attends to every source patch instead (the
plain read: keys and values flattened over S).
No label is used here. A context photo's cosine
with itself is 1, so it is among its own nearest.
N is computed once and reused by both layers.
layer 1: LabelRead (reads[0]), then norms[0] and mlps[0]
the photo's label, one copy per patch
per reading photo i: its neighbours' patches
the neighbours' labels, one per key
readers go through the attention 32 photos at a time;
memory only: the result does not depend on the chunk
q_i: the 256 patches of photo i
content decides where to look: no label so far
V flows across to the weighted sum
a soft vote: each patch's mix of its neighbours' labels
every row's photo, context and test alike
the attention has no label of its own: labels
a test photo is never a source: it cannot read
its own label. A context photo is among its
own sources and reads it (context is given).
the plain read (patch_read = "all") is the same
with N dropped: keys and values flattened over
layer 2: reads[1], norms[1], mlps[1] — identical in structure, its own weights
queries = norm_readers of layer 2 applied to layer 1's output h; keys = norm_sources of layer 2 applied to sources, and values = source_labels, both from the STAGE INPUT:
the same sources, the same source_labels and the same N as layer 1 (model.py: sources and nearest are computed once, before the loop over layers).
Same parameter count as layer 1: 132,736. Output h: (rows, 256, 128).
the row stage sees patches next to cells
all parameters of the stage (counted from the module as built by the model)
per layer: LabelRead 66,560 (two LayerNorms 512, four 128×128 linears with bias 66,048) + LayerNorm 256 + MLP 128→256→128 65,920 = 132,736
two layers 265,472 + label table E 10×128 = 1,280 = 266,752 in LabelledRead; plus the patch marker m 128 = 266,880
all trained from scratch at lr 1e-4; nothing in this stage is pretrained. The label table is the only place a label becomes a vector:
every yellow tensor above is a sum of rows of E (and, after the MLP, a function of such sums).
